message:
net: rfs: Add a BPF struct_ops hook for CPU selection

Native RFS derives the desired receive CPU from application CPU hints in
the socket flow table. There is no policy interface for choosing a
different CPU, such as another CPU in the same NUMA node.

Add a per-device bpf_rfs_ops policy under CONFIG_BPF_RFS. Invoke
select_cpu() after the native flow lookup and before the existing
migration check. Provide read-only scalar context and encode DEFAULT as
zero and an explicit CPU as CPU + 1. Validate explicit results and fall
back to the native hint when the requested CPU is invalid or offline.

Keep the native application hint, active CPU, queue progress and aRFS
state on their existing paths. Both policy proposals and fallback
decisions pass through the native migration check. Use a static key when
no policy is attached and a compile-time stub when the option is
disabled.

Require link-based attachment and CAP_NET_ADMIN in the target network
namespace. Serialize registration and replacement with RTNL, publish
policies with RCU, and wait for readers before returning from update or
unregister. Deactivate bindings on NETDEV_UNREGISTER without retaining
the device or entering the struct_ops update mutex from the notifier. An
inactive link remains inspectable until released and rejects further
updates.

Tested with an x86_64 kernel build and boot using KASAN, lockdep and RCU
checking. Building net/core/dev.o with CONFIG_BPF_RFS disabled also
passes, with no bpf_rfs references in the object. The accompanying
selftests cover receive CPU selection and link lifecycle behavior.

Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Dong Chenchen <superdcc97@163.com>

samples/bpf: Add topology-aware RFS CPU policies

The RFS struct_ops interface needs a userspace example that selects CPUs
from system topology and replaces a running policy without exposing a
partially updated configuration.

Add process, cluster and NUMA policies with candidate CPU lists and
optional SMT sibling exclusion. Parse sparse CPU lists without a fixed
64-CPU limit and represent candidates as shared groups. Keep an eligible
active CPU before hashing to another candidate. Treat the candidate pool
as a preference and fall back to native RFS when no suitable proposal is
available.

Load topology into program-read-only maps and freeze them before
attachment. Publish refreshed topology as a new program and map set
through BPF_LINK_UPDATE with expected-old-map protection. Provide
attach, update, show and detach commands for pinned links, preserving
the existing policy when replacement fails.

Add a standalone Makefile using the in-tree libbpf, bpftool and CO-RE
types. Resolve struct_ops wrapper offsets from runtime BTF when
preparing a map for a pinned-link update.

The sample builds with Clang 18 against both the new kernel BTF and an
older kernel BTF without the RFS types. Policy and pinned-link CLI tests
pass in the test-kernel VM. Hardware locality benefits and packet-
processing overhead have not been benchmarked.

Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Dong Chenchen <superdcc97@163.com>

selftests/bpf: Cover native RFS CPU selection and policy lifetime

Programmable RFS needs coverage for the CPU actually processing received
traffic as well as verifier restrictions and policy replacement.
Checking a BPF return value alone does not establish the resulting
receive CPU.

Add a dedicated bpf/rfs kselftest target. Exchange TCP traffic over
loopback and inspect SO_INCOMING_CPU while pinning the application and
sender to different CPUs. Cover native fallback, CPU zero encoding,
invalid and offline results, IPv6, application migration, and policy
replacement or detach during a connection.

Reject context writes, sleepable callbacks and reserved flags. Exercise
duplicate attachment, expected-old mismatches, device removal and
concurrent link updates. Reuse the RFS sample loader to test NUMA
migration, the cluster policy, empty candidate pools and sparse CPU-list
parsing.

Install the test wrapper, net selftest helpers and sample CLI. Run the
traffic tests in a temporary network namespace, restoring the global RFS
table size afterward. The tests require a disposable environment for CPU
hotplug, and the NUMA case requires the documented CPU layout.

All 22 tests pass in an eight-vCPU, two-node QEMU/KVM guest through
test-kernel with KASAN, lockdep and RCU checking enabled. TCP payload
checks do not establish absence of packet reordering before protocol
reassembly.

Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Dong Chenchen <superdcc97@163.com>

docs: networking: Describe BPF CPU selection for RFS

The RFS policy interface separates the desired CPU from the CPU selected
by the native migration check. Document that distinction together with
the return encoding, verifier restrictions and device attachment
lifetime.

Describe the sample build, native RFS prerequisites, topology fallback
rules and pinned-link management. Explain the sysfs remount performed by
ip netns exec and how to keep a bpffs pin accessible across commands.

Document selftest requirements and the limits of hash-based application
hints, candidate pools, CPU hotplug and TCP-based ordering checks. State
that hardware aRFS and performance require separate validation.

Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Dong Chenchen <superdcc97@163.com>
